about: Limits for an emulated WebXR session report, and adapter names that mean a software renderer. Working values chosen for mstack; none was read from a primary source. Measure on the target headset and replace them.

max_draw_calls.unit: draw calls per frame, per eye pass as reported by the renderer
max_draw_calls.source: mstack working value, no primary source
max_draw_calls.note: working value; Meta's Unity performance page (https://developers.meta.com/horizon/documentation/unity/unity-perf/) gives only example ranges (Quest 2/Pro: 80-200 draw calls in busy scenes, 750k-1m triangles; Quest 3/3S: 200-300 and 1.3m-1.8m); no source fixes a number for WebXR

max_triangles.source: mstack working value, no primary source
max_triangles.note: working value; Meta's Unity performance page (https://developers.meta.com/horizon/documentation/unity/unity-perf/) gives only example ranges (Quest 2/Pro: 80-200 draw calls in busy scenes, 750k-1m triangles; Quest 3/3S: 200-300 and 1.3m-1.8m); no source fixes a number for WebXR

software_renderers.unit: lower-case fragments of a GPU adapter name
software_renderers.source: mstack working list, no primary source
software_renderers.note: working list; adapter names are not standardised
